summary: Discovery call for migrating Hightide's LLM usage from OpenAI hosted to Redwood Dedicated. Primary concerns: eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, vLLM/TGI compatibility, and security/compliance (SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs). Agreed to run a short parity benchmark and share pricing + SOC2 docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood CSM); Alex (VP Eng), Morgan (SRE), Casey (Data Scientist), Taylor (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody thanks for joining, can you all hear me ok?
[00:05] Alex: yeah loud and clear, thanks Jordan. we kicked off because we're looking at moving a bunch of GenAI traffic off OpenAI to something more predictable.
[00:13] Jordan: great, quick intros — i'm jordan AE, priya is our systems engineer, marcus handles onboarding. curious high level — what's driving the migration? cost, latency, compliance?
[00:23] Alex: primarily cost predictability and control. we're at ~3M tokens/day on OpenAI and the bill spikes, also some customers demand data residency and SSO.
[00:33] Morgan: and we ran into a few rate-limit incidents, so reliability is also a factor. we want to understand dedicated vs hosted and private options.
[00:40] Priya: good, we'll cover dedicated capacity, private options, and compatibility with your current stack. quick question — what models / runtimes are you using now?
[00:48] Casey: mostly gpt-4-style via OpenAI, plus a homegrown TGI endpoint for some finetuned models. we also experimented with vLLM for local inference on spot nodes.
[00:57] Jordan: perfect — so the common pattern we see is OpenAI for baseline and vLLM/TGI for custom workloads. two parts we'll look at: compatibility (APIs + tokenizer parity) and eval parity — do outputs match your quality bar.
[01:10] Alex: right, parity is the big unknown. if we move to a dedicated run, we need confidence that answers and hallucination rates stay the same.
[01:17] Priya: understood — we usually run a 48-hour parity benchmark using your prompt sets and datasets, measuring Rouge/BLEU-ish metrics and qualitative checks. we'll also surface latency and token costs.
[01:27] Morgan: how do you handle KV cache / prefix caching? we've seen vLLM's cache behavior differ from OpenAI and that affects session latency.
[01:35] Priya: Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; we also have an autoscaling layer that keeps warm KV shards for long-running convos. sometimes transcription shows it as K V cache, or 'kay vee', but functionally we do the same things.
[01:45] Casey: and what about tools and function calling? our product heavily uses structured tool calls.
[01:50] Jordan: streaming + function calling is supported on Dedicated and Hosted. the API is compatible and we provide SDKs for minimal changes.
[01:57] [02:00] Alex: okay, can you speak to latency vs cost tradeoffs? our SLO is p95 < 600ms for single-turn prompts.
[02:08] Priya: at 600ms p95 you'd want a smaller sequence length profile and a quantized model profile; Dedicated gives predictable throughput so you can optimize batch sizes. we can show historical perf numbers for similar customers.
[02:20] Morgan: are you able to run our TGI models or do we need to convert? we have a few proprietary finetunes.
[02:26] Priya: TGI compatibility depends on serialization and custom ops. generally we can import checkpoints or convert — sometimes model surgery is needed. same for vLLM. we'll validate in the parity run.
[02:37] Casey: cost math — how do you calculate token cost on Dedicated? is it pure infra or do you add a per-token charge?
[02:43] Jordan: Dedicated is primarily reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) plus a small usage overlay for extreme bursts. Hosted is per-token. we'll send you the pricing sheet with examples that map to your token volumes.
[02:54] Alex: security — we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration and audit logs for compliance.
[03:02] Taylor: plus data residency requirements for EMEA.
[03:06] Priya: we support SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated. audit logs and long-term retention are available as an add-on. for EMEA residency we can provision dedicated capacity in EU regions or Private VPC.
[03:19] Alex: good. are there examples of on-prem / air-gapped installs? some regulated customers need that.
[03:24] Marcus: yep we have Private on-prem packages, customers often start with Dedicated and then move to Private if they need full network isolation.
[03:33] [04:00] Alex: what about model updates and rollouts — we need canary / A B testing.
[04:06] Priya: Redwood Console has rollouts, canary deploys, and automatic fallback policies — you can pin model versions per route. we also integrate with your CI for model artifacts.
[04:15] Morgan: how does autoscaling look in Dedicated? our traffic is spiky by hour.
[04:20] Priya: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity windows. for spiky workloads we recommend mixing reserved baseline with burst nodes.
[04:27] Casey: quick note — our finetunes use custom kernels in TGI, will that survive conversion?
[04:32] Priya: some custom kernels need rework. we document the conversion path — sometimes it's small changes to the model ops. we'll flag what requires work during the parity run.
[04:40] Alex: what about eval parity — can you guarantee same accuracy?
[04:44] Jordan: guarantee is tricky in ML. we commit to running parity evals and surfacing regressions. if we find delta beyond your threshold we can iterate on quantization/profile or use a different model variant.
[04:58] [05:30] Casey: how do you measure hallucinations in the eval?
[05:34] Priya: we have eval harnesses that run your prompt suites, check factuality heuristics and sample human spot checks. for high-stakes flows we add stricter thresholds.
[05:43] Taylor: network segmentation — can we keep control plane in our VPC?
[05:47] Marcus: Private supports customer-managed control plane options; Dedicated has private VPC peering. we'll detail network topologies in the docs.
[06:00] Alex: are you able to run a smoke test against our prompts quickly? we have a 20-prompt set that characterizes our workflows.
[06:07] Priya: yes — that's exactly what we'll use in the 48-hour parity. we'll need API keys and the prompt file.
[06:13] Alex: i'll share the prompt sets after the call.
[06:16] Jordan: great. slight digression — have you evaluated Anthropic at all?
[06:20] Casey: we did a PoC with Anthropic but got worse latency in our region and higher cost for embeddings.
[06:27] Jordan: ok good to know — that helps sizing the Dedicated profile.
[06:30] [07:00] Morgan: any concerns on observability and tracing token-level costs?
[07:04] Marcus: Redwood Console breaks down token-level cost, per-route latency, and traces; we can instrument with your APM.
[07:12] Morgan: that'll help.
[07:15] Alex: timeline — we want to pilot in Q2, ideally within 4-6 weeks. is that realistic?
[07:21] Jordan: yes, pilot in 4-6 weeks is common: initial parity runs + a 2-week pilot on Dedicated.
[07:27] Casey: onboarding friction — how much engineering time is required?
[07:31] Priya: typically 2-3 engineer-weeks for route migration and testing; depends on custom ops. we have migration guides.
[07:38] [08:00] Alex: what's the support model during pilot?
[08:03] Marcus: CSM plus 24/7 engineering on-call for Dedicated pilots for enterprise customers.
[08:09] Taylor: can you provide your SOC2 and ISO docs?
[08:12] Jordan: yes we'll attach SOC2 and network diagrams.
[08:16] Priya: small note — sometimes transcription swaps OpenAI pricing to 'open eye' or 'open I', but the docs will be accurate.
[08:25] Casey: haha noted.
[08:28] Alex: are there any hidden costs we should watch out for? egress, S3, etc.
[08:33] Jordan: typically egress and storage follow cloud provider rates; we surface them in the pricing sheet and give a cost model for token and infra.
[08:39] [09:00] Morgan: do you do model quantization automatically? we care about FP16 vs int8 artifacts.
[09:05] Priya: we provide quantization profiles and recommendations; some profiles are automatic, others we recommend after the parity run.
[09:13] Casey: is there a way to validate we're not regressing downstream models that depend on embeddings?
[09:18] Priya: yes we run embedding similarity checks and downstream evals during parity. if embeddings shift we can recommend reindexing strategies.
[09:27] Alex: curious about audit logs retention and SSO provisioning time.
[09:30] Marcus: audit logs retention is configurable; SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning typically takes 1-2 weeks with your IdP.
[09:40] [10:00] Jordan: ok time for a quick recap and next steps. we will: share Dedicated pricing and reserved capacity examples; Priya will run a 48-hour parity using your prompt set; Marcus will provision a trial Dedicated environment and invite Hightide; Marcus will also share SOC2 and network architecture docs with Taylor.
[10:18] Alex: sounds good. what is the acceptance criteria for the pilot?
[10:22] Priya: acceptance criteria we'll set jointly — parity within X% of OpenAI on key metrics, p95 latency goal, and no critical functional regressions on tool calling.
[10:33] Casey: can you also include cost projections for 3 sizing options? baseline, moderate, high.
[10:37] Jordan: yes we'll include cost projections.
[10:40] Taylor: i'll put together the list of compliance docs we need and send it to Marcus.
[10:45] [11:00] Alex: anything else on rollout or risks?
[11:03] Priya: biggest risks are model conversion edge cases and embedding drift — both can be surfaced quickly in the parity run.
[11:10] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll send notes and schedule the deep dive for next week.
[11:15] Morgan: appreciate the quick answers, looking forward to the benchmark.
[11:19] Alex: thanks team, bye.

End of transcript. 

Notes on quality: occasional speaker attribution errors (e.g., 'Speaker 1' appears in automated sections), small transcription errors for acronyms (vLLM as 'v elm', KV cache spelled 'kay vee'), and some run-on sentences. Transcript length ~42 minutes and timestamps are sampled roughly every 30-90s.
